functions.name: xls_open_file
functions.signature: xlsWorkBook* xls_open_file(const char *file, const char *charset, xls_error_t *outError);
functions.description: Opens an Excel (XLS) file from the filesystem and returns a workbook handle. Converts internal 16-bit strings to the specified 8-bit encoding (UTF-8 by default). On failure, returns NULL and optionally sets outError.

charset may be NULL or a valid encoding name understood by libxls; when NULL, library default (UTF-8) is used (per comment).
outError may be NULL or a non-NULL pointer where an xls_error_t will be stored on failure; caller should initialize/inspect as needed.

functions.name: xls_open_buffer

functions.description: Opens an Excel (XLS) workbook from an in-memory buffer. Converts internal 16-bit strings to the specified 8-bit encoding (UTF-8 by default). Returns a workbook handle or NULL on failure and optionally sets outError.
requirements: data must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer containing the entire XLS file image.
data_len must be the exact size in bytes of the data buffer and greater than 0.
charset may be NULL or a valid encoding name understood by libxls; when NULL, library default (UTF-8) is used (per comment).
outError may be NULL or a non-NULL pointer where an xls_error_t will be stored on failure; caller should inspect on error.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use and must later close the workbook with xls_close_WB.

functions.name: xls_close_WB
functions.description: Closes and frees resources associated with a workbook returned by libxls open functions.

pWB may be NULL if the implementation permits; if non-NULL it must not be reused after closing. Behavior on double-close is unspecified.

Caller must check for NULL return and close the workbook later with xls_close_WB.

functions.name: xls_close
functions.description: Closes and frees an xlsWorkBook handle. This is the historical API name xls_close, which is a macro alias to xls_close_WB. Use it to release resources for a workbook opened via xls_open_file, xls_open_buffer, or the legacy xls_open.
requirements: pWB must be a valid xlsWorkBook* previously obtained from xls_open_file, xls_open_buffer, or xls_open.

data_types.description: A valid Microsoft Excel binary workbook (BIFF) file image. When provided via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, the path points to a file containing raw XLS bytes. When provided via FUZZ_PARAM_STR to a buffer-based open, the string’s raw bytes are treated as the complete XLS file content. Expected to follow BIFF structures for Excel 2.x–8.0 (e.g., BOF/EOF records, Workbook stream, etc.). May include OLE2 container if required by the format.

An ASCII/UTF-8 string naming a character set/encoding understood by the library for converting internal 16-bit strings to 8-bit (e.g., "UTF-8", "ISO-8859-1", "Windows-1252"). The string may also be NULL to request the library default.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator builds minimal-yet-valid OLE2 (CFBF) compound files containing a Workbook stream
# with a minimal BIFF8 workbook (BOF/EOF). The output bytes can be used either as a filename-backed
# file (FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME) or as an in-memory buffer (FUZZ_PARAM_STR) for xls::xls_open_buffer.
#
# Goals:
# - Produce valid Compound File header, FAT, MiniFAT, and Directory so readers accept it.
# - Provide a Workbook stream name common in XLS: "Workbook" (BIFF8) and optionally variations like
#   "Book" or embedded SummaryInformation to trigger different code paths.
# - Insert minimal BIFF stream: BOF (Workbook globals), EOF; optionally a worksheet substream to
#   encourage deeper parsing when the library follows SHEET records (kept optional to stay small).
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# References for constants:
# - CFBF header signature D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1
# - Sector size = 512 (sector_shift = 9)
# - Mini sector size = 64 (mini_sector_shift = 6)
# - DIFAT array in header holds up to 109 FAT sector indices
# - Directory entry size = 128 bytes
# - End-of-chain marker 0xFFFFFFFE, Free 0xFFFFFFFF, FAT 0xFFFFFFFD, DIFAT 0xFFFFFFFC
#
# BIFF8 minimal workbook stream records:
# - BOF (0x0809) with type Workbook globals (0x0005)
# - EOF (0x000A)
# Optionally add BOUNDSHEET (0x0085) pointing to a minimal worksheet substream (BOF type 0x0010, EOF)

FREE = 0xFFFFFFFF
FATSECT = 0xFFFFFFFD
ENDOFCHAIN = 0xFFFFFFFE
DIFSECT = 0xFFFFFFFC

SECTOR_SIZE = 512
MINI_SECTOR_SIZE = 64
DIR_ENTRY_SIZE = 128

# Utilities

def align_up(x: int, a: int) -> int:
    return (x + a - 1) // a * a


def u32le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def u16le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)


def make_biff_workbook(include_sheet: bool, codepage: int) -> Tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    # Build Workbook stream and optional Worksheet stream
    records: List[bytes] = []

    # BIFF record helper
    def rec(rid: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        return struct.pack('<HH', rid, len(payload)) + payload

    # BOF Workbook Globals (0x0809)
    # version = 0x0600 (BIFF8), type=0x0005, build=0x0DBB, year=0x07CC, flags=0x0001, minvers=0x0000
    bof_payload = struct.pack('<HHHHHH', 0x0600, 0x0005, 0x0DBB, 0x07CC, 0x0001, 0x0000)
    records.append(rec(0x0809, bof_payload))

    # CODEPAGE (0x0042) to control charset conversion paths (e.g., 1200 UTF-16LE is uncommon in XLS, use 1252)
    records.append(rec(0x0042, u16le(codepage)))

    # WINDOW1 (0x003D) minimal payload
    records.append(rec(0x003D, struct.pack('<HHHHHH', 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)))

    worksheet_stream = b''
    if include_sheet:
        # Build a minimal worksheet substream
        ws_recs: List[bytes] = []
        ws_bof = struct.pack('<HHHHHH', 0x0600, 0x0010, 0x0DBB, 0x07CC, 0x0001, 0x0000)
        ws_recs.append(rec(0x0809, ws_bof))
        # DIMENSIONS (0x0200): rows [0,1), cols [0,1)
        ws_recs.append(rec(0x0200, struct.pack('<I I H H H', 0, 1, 0, 1, 0)))
        # EOF
        ws_recs.append(rec(0x000A, b''))
        worksheet_stream = b''.join(ws_recs)

        # BOUNDSHEET points to offset within Workbook stream where the worksheet BOF starts
        # We'll place BOUNDSHEET now with a placeholder, but easier is to append BOUNDSHEET before EOF
        # and compute offset as current length plus size of remaining records in globals (EOF only).
        # Offset is relative to start of Workbook stream.
        ws_offset = 0  # placeholder; compute after we know length of globals up to BOUNDSHEET
        # We will compute after assembling.
        pass

    # If including sheet, we need to add BOUNDSHEET with correct offset just before EOF of workbook globals
    if include_sheet:
        # Current length so far in workbook globals
        globals_prefix = b''.join(records)
        # The worksheet substream will be appended after the globals EOF, so its offset equals
        # len(globals_prefix) + len(EOF record to be added next).
        eof_len = 4  # header for EOF (rid+len) + 0 payload = 4 bytes
        ws_offset = len(globals_prefix) + eof_len
        # BOUNDSHEET payload: offset (DWORD), sheet state/visibility (byte), sheet type (byte=0x00 worksheet), name (XLUnicodeString)
        # Use ANSI short name 'Sheet1'
        name = b'Sheet1'
        name_len = len(name)
        payload = struct.pack('<I B B', ws_offset, 0x00, 0x00) + struct.pack('<B', name_len) + name
        records.append(rec(0x0085, payload))

    # EOF for workbook globals
    records.append(rec(0x000A, b''))

    wb_stream = b''.join(records)
    if include_sheet:
        wb_stream += worksheet_stream

    return wb_stream, worksheet_stream


def build_directory(entries: List[Tuple[str, int, int, int]]) -> bytes:
    # entries: list of (name, obj_type, start_sector, stream_size)
    # obj_type: 5=root storage, 2=stream, 1=storage
    dir_bytes = b''
    for i, (name, obj_type, start_sector, size) in enumerate(entries):
        # Name in UTF-16LE, null-terminated; name_len includes terminating null in bytes
        name_utf16 = (name + '\x00').encode('utf-16le')
        name_len = len(name_utf16)
        name_utf16 = name_utf16.ljust(64, b'\x00')  # 32 WCHARs = 64 bytes
        # sibling/child pointers: no red-black tree used here
        entry = name_utf16
        entry += u16le(name_len)
        entry += bytes([obj_type])
        entry += bytes([0])  # color (black)
        entry += u32le(0xFFFFFFFF)  # left sibling
        entry += u32le(0xFFFFFFFF)  # right sibling
        # child: for root, we set to 0xFFFFFFFF (no child); simple flat directory
        entry += u32le(0xFFFFFFFF)
        # CLSID (16 bytes)
        entry += b'\x00' * 16
        # state bits
        entry += u32le(0)
        # creation and modified times (8+8 bytes)
        entry += b'\x00' * 8
        entry += b'\x00' * 8
        # start sector
        entry += u32le(start_sector if start_sector is not None else 0xFFFFFFFF)
        # stream size (QWORD)
        entry += struct.pack('<Q', size if size is not None else 0)
        dir_bytes += entry.ljust(DIR_ENTRY_SIZE, b'\x00')
    # Ensure directory size is multiple of sector size by padding; done by caller per sector write
    return dir_bytes


def build_cfbf_with_streams(streams: List[Tuple[str, bytes]]) -> bytes:
    # streams: list of (name, data). Includes Root entry which has mini stream when needed.
    # We will place all streams in regular FAT sectors (>= 4096 threshold for mini stream). Since our sizes
    # are small, classic spec uses mini stream for < 4096, but to keep implementation simple and robust for
    # many readers, we put them in normal FAT and leave mini stream unused. This is acceptable and commonly supported.
    sector_size = SECTOR_SIZE

    # Layout plan:
    # sector 0: Header (512 bytes, not a sector in FAT index space; FAT indexing starts at 0 for first sector after header)
    # sector 0 (after header) -> Directory
    # sector 1 -> Stream 0 (Workbook)
    # sector 2 -> Stream 1 (optional SummaryInformation or additional stream)
    # FAT sectors count chosen so FAT covers allocated sectors

    # Build directory entries list; root entry must exist
    # We'll add Root Entry, Workbook, and optional SummaryInformation
    dir_entries = []  # will be filled after sectors assigned

    # Assign sectors sequentially after directory; compute sizes in sectors
    # We'll decide order: place Directory at sector 0, streams after.

    # Prepare streams padded to sector boundaries
    stream_datas = [data for (_, data) in streams]
    stream_sizes = [len(d) for d in stream_datas]
    stream_padded = [d + b'\x00' * (align_up(len(d), sector_size) - len(d)) for d in stream_datas]
    stream_sec_counts = [len(p) // sector_size for p in stream_padded]

    # Directory size: number of entries = root + len(streams)
    num_dir_entries = 1 + len(streams)
    dir_bytes = build_directory([])  # placeholder
    # compute dir sectors needed
    dir_bytes_size = num_dir_entries * DIR_ENTRY_SIZE
    dir_padded_size = align_up(dir_bytes_size, sector_size)
    dir_sectors = dir_padded_size // sector_size

    # Sector indices (in FAT space) start at 0 for the first 512-byte sector after the header.
    dir_start_sector = 0
    next_sector = dir_start_sector + dir_sectors

    stream_start_sectors = []
    for sc in stream_sec_counts:
        stream_start_sectors.append(next_sector if sc > 0 else 0xFFFFFFFF)
        next_sector += sc

    total_sectors_no_fat = next_sector

    # FAT needs to have entries for all allocated sectors and mark FAT sectors themselves.
    # Compute FAT sectors count. Each FAT sector holds 128 FAT entries (512/4).
    def fat_needed(n_entries: int) -> int:
        return (n_entries + 127) // 128

    # We need entries for: all data sectors (directory + streams) + FAT sectors themselves
    data_sectors = total_sectors_no_fat
    fat_sectors = 0
    while True:
        entries = data_sectors + fat_sectors
        need = fat_needed(entries)
        if need == fat_sectors:
            break
        fat_sectors = need
    total_sectors = data_sectors + fat_sectors

    # Now build FAT table entries
    fat: List[int] = [FREE] * total_sectors

    # Chain directory sectors
    for i in range(dir_sectors):
        idx = dir_start_sector + i
        fat[idx] = (idx + 1) if i < dir_sectors - 1 else ENDOFCHAIN

    # Chain each stream sectors
    for s_idx, sc in enumerate(stream_sec_counts):
        if sc == 0:
            continue
        start = stream_start_sectors[s_idx]
        for i in range(sc):
            idx = start + i
            fat[idx] = (idx + 1) if i < sc - 1 else ENDOFCHAIN

    # Mark FAT sectors as FATSECT at the end of the space
    fat_sector_indices = list(range(total_sectors - fat_sectors, total_sectors))
    for idx in fat_sector_indices:
        fat[idx] = FATSECT

    # Build directory bytes now with proper entries
    dir_entries = []
    # Root entry: start sector = 0xFFFFFFFF, size 0 when no mini stream
    dir_entries.append(('Root Entry', 5, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0))
    for (name, _data), start, size in zip(streams, stream_start_sectors, stream_sizes):
        dir_entries.append((name, 2, start, size))
    dir_bytes = build_directory(dir_entries)
    dir_bytes = dir_bytes.ljust(dir_sectors * sector_size, b'\x00')

    # Build FAT sectors content
    fat_bytes = b''.join(u32le(x) for x in fat)
    fat_bytes = fat_bytes.ljust(fat_sectors * sector_size, b'\x00')

    # Build header
    header = b''
    header += bytes.fromhex('D0CF11E0A1B11AE1')  # signature
    header += bytes.fromhex('0000000000000000')  # clsid
    header += u16le(0x003E)  # minor
    header += u16le(0x0003)  # dll version (3 => 512-byte sectors)
    header += u16le(0xFFFE)  # byte order
    header += u16le(9)       # sector shift (2^9 = 512)
    header += u16le(6)       # mini sector shift (2^6 = 64)
    header += b'\x00' * 6   # reserved
    header += u32le(fat_sectors)  # number of FAT sectors
    header += u32le(dir_start_sector)  # first directory sector location
    header += u32le(0)       # transaction signature (unused)
    header += u32le(4096)    # mini stream cutoff size
    header += u32le(0xFFFFFFFF)  # first mini FAT sector (none)
    header += u32le(0)       # mini FAT sector count
    header += u32le(0xFFFFFFFF)  # first DIFAT sector (none)
    header += u32le(0)       # DIFAT count
    # DIFAT array (109 entries); when FAT sectors exist, list their sector indices here
    difat = [FREE] * 109
    for i, idx in enumerate(fat_sector_indices[:109]):
        difat[i] = idx
    header += b''.join(u32le(x) for x in difat)
    header = header.ljust(512, b'\x00')

    # Assemble file: header + directory + streams + FAT
    file_bytes = header
    file_bytes += dir_bytes
    for p in stream_padded:
        file_bytes += p
    file_bytes += fat_bytes

    return file_bytes


def build_summary_info(title: str, author: str) -> bytes:
    # Minimal property set stream for \x05SummaryInformation is optional; include a tiny valid header
    # to tick summary parsing paths. Build very small variant with PIDSI_TITLE (2) and PIDSI_AUTHOR (4).
    # This is a simplified and should be acceptable to tolerant parsers.
    FMTID_Summary = bytes.fromhex('E0859FF2F94F6810AB9108002B27B3D9')  # FMTID_SummaryInformation
    CLSID_Null = b'\x00' * 16

    def pad4(b: bytes) -> bytes:
        return b + (b'\x00' * ((4 - (len(b) % 4)) % 4))

    # Build property section
    props = []
    # Title (PID 2) VT_LPSTR = 0x1E
    t_bytes = title.encode('utf-8')[:128]
    p2 = struct.pack('<I', 0x1E) + struct.pack('<I', len(t_bytes) + 1) + t_bytes + b'\x00'
    p2 = pad4(p2)
    props.append((2, p2))
    # Author (PID 4)
    a_bytes = author.encode('utf-8')[:128]
    p4 = struct.pack('<I', 0x1E) + struct.pack('<I', len(a_bytes) + 1) + a_bytes + b'\x00'
    p4 = pad4(p4)
    props.append((4, p4))

    num_props = len(props)
    # Offset table follows section header (8 + 8 + 4 + (num_props*8) + prop data)
    # Build section header: FMTID + offset (we'll set to 0x30 after header) but using one section only.
    # Property set stream header
    header = struct.pack('<I', 0xFEFF0000)  # byte order + version/minor
    header += struct.pack('<I', 0x00000000)  # OS/format
    header += struct.pack('<I', 1)  # section count
    header += FMTID_Summary
    header += struct.pack('<I', 0x30)  # section offset immediately after this header (0x30)

    # Section: CLSID + property count + property list
    section = CLSID_Null
    section += struct.pack('<I', num_props)
    # Build property list with offsets
    offset = 8 + 4 + num_props * 8  # after CLSID + count + entries
    prop_list = b''
    payload = b''
    current = offset
    for pid, pdata in props:
        prop_list += struct.pack('<I', pid) + struct.pack('<I', current)
        payload += pdata
        current += len(pdata)
    section += prop_list + payload
    return header + section


def build_valid_xls(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly decide to include a worksheet to drive worksheet parsing paths
    include_sheet = rng.choice([True, False, True])  # bias to True
    # Choose a common Windows codepage to exercise charset parameter
    codepage = rng.choice([1252, 65001, 1250, 1251]) if not include_sheet else rng.choice([1252, 1252, 1252, 65001])

    wb_stream, _ = make_biff_workbook(include_sheet, codepage)

    streams: List[Tuple[str, bytes]] = []
    # Primary workbook stream name for BIFF8 is "Workbook"; some files use "Book". Prefer Workbook.
    workbook_name = rng.choice(["Workbook", "Workbook", "Book"])
    streams.append((workbook_name, wb_stream))

    # Optionally add SummaryInformation stream to exercise summary parser
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        title = rng.choice(["Fuzz Workbook", "Test", "Sample", "BIFF8"])
        author = rng.choice(["libxls", "tester", "user"]) 
        sum_stream = build_summary_info(title, author)
        streams.append(("\x05SummaryInformation", sum_stream))

    cfbf = build_cfbf_with_streams(streams)
    # Ensure final size <= 4096; if larger due to streams, truncate is invalid, so instead, if too large,
    # rebuild without optional streams.
    if len(cfbf) > 4096:
        streams = [(workbook_name, wb_stream)]
        cfbf = build_cfbf_with_streams(streams)
    return cfbf


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    return build_valid_xls(seed)

import random
import struct

# Goal: Generate diverse, valid inputs for libxls fuzzers.
# - For FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME / open_file and open_buffer: produce valid XLS (OLE2/CFB + BIFF8) images.
# - For FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as charset: produce plausible, varied encoding names.
# The generator must be seeded yet yield many unique outputs across seeds.
# Keep outputs <=4096 bytes and self-contained.

# Helpers

def _u16(v):
    return struct.pack('<H', v)

def _u32(v):
    return struct.pack('<I', v)

# BIFF record helper

def biff_record(rtype, payload=b""):
    return _u16(rtype) + _u16(len(payload)) + payload

# Build a small variety of BIFF8 workbook streams with variability:
# - Different sheet counts (1..2)
# - Different cell contents (NUMBER, LABELSST), sizes
# - Different codepage values
# - Different sheet names
# - Optional SST, optional WRITEACCESS

def build_biff8_workbook(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    RT_BOF = 0x0809
    RT_EOF = 0x000A
    RT_BOUNDSHEET = 0x0085
    RT_WRITEACCESS = 0x005C
    RT_CODEPAGE = 0x0042
    RT_SST = 0x00FC
    RT_LABELSST = 0x00FD
    RT_DIMENSIONS = 0x0200
    RT_NUMBER = 0x0203

    # Workbook BOF
    build_id = 0x0DBB
    build_year = 0x07CC
    bof_wb = biff_record(
        RT_BOF,
        _u16(0x0600) + _u16(0x0005) + _u16(build_id) + _u16(build_year) + _u32(0x00000041),
    )

    # Varied codepages
    codepages = [1252, 65001, 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1251, 1250]
    codepage = biff_record(RT_CODEPAGE, _u16(rng.choice(codepages)))

    wa = b""
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # WRITEACCESS: 112 bytes, fill with ASCII name padded
        name = ("Fuzzer" + str(seed % 1000)).encode('ascii')
        wa = biff_record(RT_WRITEACCESS, (name + b"\x00" * 112)[:112])

    # SST variability
    use_sst = rng.random() < 0.9
    sst = b""
    sst_strings = []
    if use_sst:
        base_strings = [
            b"Hello",
            b"Charset UTF-8",
            b"LibXLS",
            b"Sheet",
            ("Seed" + str(seed)).encode('ascii'),
        ]
        # choose 1..3 strings
        sst_strings = rng.sample(base_strings, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(base_strings))))
        sst_items = b""
        for s in sst_strings:
            # compressed 8-bit flag 0x00
            sst_items += _u16(len(s)) + b"\x00" + s
        sst = biff_record(RT_SST, _u32(len(sst_strings)) + _u32(len(sst_strings)) + sst_items)

    # Prepare worksheets (1..2)
    sheet_count = 1 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 2

    # Pre-build worksheet streams to compute offsets
    ws_streams = []
    sheet_names = []

    for si in range(sheet_count):
        # Worksheet BOF
        bof_ws = biff_record(
            RT_BOF,
            _u16(0x0600) + _u16(0x0010) + _u16(build_id) + _u16(build_year) + _u32(0x00000041),
        )
        # Dimensions 2..5 rows/cols
        rows = rng.randint(2, 5)
        cols = rng.randint(2, 5)
        dims = biff_record(RT_DIMENSIONS, _u32(0) + _u32(rows) + _u16(0) + _u16(cols) + _u16(0))

        cells = []
        # Add one NUMBER
        value = rng.choice([0.0, 1.0, 3.14, 42.0, -1.0, seed % 97])
        cells.append(biff_record(RT_NUMBER, _u16(0) + _u16(0) + _u16(0) + struct.pack('<d', float(value))))
        # Optionally one LABELSST
        if use_sst and sst_strings and rng.random() < 0.9:
            sst_ix = rng.randrange(len(sst_strings))
            cells.append(biff_record(RT_LABELSST, _u16(0) + _u16(1) + _u16(0) + _u32(sst_ix)))
        eof_ws = biff_record(RT_EOF)
        ws_stream = bof_ws + dims + b"".join(cells) + eof_ws
        ws_streams.append(ws_stream)

        # Sheet name variety (<=31 chars, ASCII compressed)
        base_name = rng.choice(["Sheet", "Data", "Лист", "工作表", "Feuille"])  # will be ASCII fallback
        ascii_name = (base_name + str(1 + si))
        # ensure ASCII bytes
        ascii_bytes = ascii_name.encode('ascii', errors='ignore') or (b"Sheet" + bytes([48 + si]))
        sheet_names.append(ascii_bytes[:31])

    # Build workbook globals without BOUNDSHEET first
    wb_prefix = bof_wb + codepage + wa + sst

    # Build provisional boundsheets to compute lbPlyPos later
    boundsheets = []
    for name_bytes in sheet_names:
        name_field = bytes([len(name_bytes)]) + b"\x00" + name_bytes  # compressed short name
        bs_payload = _u32(0) + b"\x00\x00\x00" + name_field
        boundsheets.append(biff_record(RT_BOUNDSHEET, bs_payload))

    eof_wb = biff_record(RT_EOF)

    # Compute positions: Workbook stream layout = wb_prefix + sum(boundsheets_patched) + eof_wb + concat(ws_streams)
    # First compute size of wb_prefix + boundsheets_patched (unknown lbPlyPos) + eof_wb
    temp = wb_prefix + b"".join(boundsheets) + eof_wb
    # lbPlyPos for sheet i is len(wb_prefix + all_boundsheets_patched + eof_wb + all previous ws streams)
    patched_bounds = []
    ws_prefix_len = len(temp)
    running = ws_prefix_len
    for i, name_bytes in enumerate(sheet_names):
        lbPlyPos = running
        name_field = bytes([len(name_bytes)]) + b"\x00" + name_bytes
        bs_payload = _u32(lbPlyPos) + b"\x00\x00\x00" + name_field
        patched_bounds.append(biff_record(RT_BOUNDSHEET, bs_payload))
        running += len(ws_streams[i])

    wb_stream = wb_prefix + b"".join(patched_bounds) + eof_wb + b"".join(ws_streams)
    return wb_stream

# Build a minimal OLE2/CFB container with a stream named "Workbook" containing the BIFF stream.

def build_min_cfb_with_workbook(workbook_bytes):
    SECTOR_SIZE = 512

    def pad_to_sector(b):
        rem = len(b) % SECTOR_SIZE
        if rem:
            b += b"\x00" * (SECTOR_SIZE - rem)
        return b

    wb_data = pad_to_sector(workbook_bytes)
    num_wb_sectors = len(wb_data) // SECTOR_SIZE

    # Sector indices
    # 0: FAT, 1..N: Workbook, N+1: Directory
    wb_first_sec = 1
    dir_sec = 1 + num_wb_sectors

    total_sectors = 1 + num_wb_sectors + 1

    # FAT entries (128 entries per FAT sector)
    FAT = []
    FAT.append(0xFFFFFFFD)  # sector 0 is FAT itself
    for i in range(num_wb_sectors):
        FAT.append(wb_first_sec + i + 1 if i < num_wb_sectors - 1 else 0xFFFFFFFE)
    FAT.append(0xFFFFFFFE)  # directory end of chain
    while len(FAT) < 128:
        FAT.append(0xFFFFFFFF)
    fat_sector = b"".join(_u32(x & 0xFFFFFFFF) for x in FAT)

    # Header
    header = bytearray(512)
    header[0:8] = b"\xD0\xCF\x11\xE0\xA1\xB1\x1A\xE1"
    header[8:24] = b"\x00" * 16
    header[24:26] = struct.pack('<H', 0x003E)  # minor
    header[26:28] = struct.pack('<H', 0x0003)  # major (512b)
    header[28:30] = struct.pack('<H', 0xFFFE)  # byte order
    header[30:32] = struct.pack('<H', 0x0009)  # sector shift
    header[32:34] = struct.pack('<H', 0x0006)  # mini sector shift
    header[34:44] = b"\x00" * 10
    header[44:48] = _u32(0)
    header[48:52] = _u32(1)  # FAT sector count
    header[52:56] = _u32(0xFFFFFFFF)  # first DIFAT
    header[56:60] = _u32(0)
    header[60:64] = _u32(dir_sec)  # first directory sector
    header[64:68] = _u32(0)
    header[68:72] = _u32(0x1000)
    header[72:76] = _u32(0xFFFFFFFF)  # mini FAT first
    header[76:80] = _u32(0)
    header[80:84] = _u32(0xFFFFFFFF)  # DIFAT first
    header[84:88] = _u32(0)
    # Header DIFAT entries: first FAT sector index (0)
    header[76+8:76+12] = _u32(0)

    # Directory stream: Root Entry + Workbook stream entry
    def dir_entry(name_utf16le, obj_type, color, left, right, child, clsid, state_bits, creation, modified, start_sector, stream_size):
        name_bytes = name_utf16le + b"\x00\x00"
        name_len = len(name_bytes)
        name_field = name_bytes + b"\x00" * (64 - name_len)
        entry = bytearray(128)
        entry[0:64] = name_field
        entry[64:66] = _u16(name_len)
        entry[66] = obj_type
        entry[67] = color
        entry[68:72] = _u32(left)
        entry[72:76] = _u32(right)
        entry[76:80] = _u32(child)
        entry[80:96] = b"\x00" * 16
        entry[96:100] = _u32(state_bits)
        entry[100:108] = b"\x00" * 8
        entry[108:116] = b"\x00" * 8
        entry[116:120] = _u32(start_sector)
        entry[120:128] = struct.pack('<Q', stream_size)
        return bytes(entry)

    root = dir_entry("Root Entry".encode('utf-16le'), 5, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, b"\x00" * 16, 0, b"\x00" * 8, b"\x00" * 8, 0xFFFFFFFF, len(wb_data))
    workbook = dir_entry("Workbook".encode('utf-16le'), 2, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, b"\x00" * 16, 0, b"\x00" * 8, b"\x00" * 8, wb_first_sec, len(wb_data))
    dir_stream = root + workbook
    # pad directory to sector
    if len(dir_stream) % SECTOR_SIZE:
        dir_stream += b"\x00" * (SECTOR_SIZE - (len(dir_stream) % SECTOR_SIZE))

    return bytes(header) + fat_sector + wb_data + dir_stream

# Charset pool with expanded variety and minor randomization
CHARSETS = [
    b"UTF-8", b"utf-8", b"UTF8", b"utf8", b"UTF_8",
    b"ISO-8859-1", b"iso-8859-1", b"latin1", b"Latin-1",
    b"Windows-1252", b"windows-1252", b"cp1252", b"CP1252",
    b"Shift_JIS", b"shift_jis", b"SJIS", b"sjis",
    b"GB18030", b"gb18030", b"GBK", b"gbk", b"Big5", b"big5",
    b"KOI8-R", b"koi8-r", b"ISO-8859-5", b"iso-8859-5",
    b"MacRoman", b"macroman", b"ASCII", b"ascii", b"CP437", b"cp437", b"CP850", b"cp850",
]

# Slight randomized decoration to increase uniqueness while staying plausible.

def tweak_charset(rng, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    s = bytearray(base)
    # Random case tweaks
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = bytearray(bytes([ord(chr(c).upper()) if 97 <= c <= 122 else c for c in s]))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = bytearray(bytes([ord(chr(c).lower()) if 65 <= c <= 90 else c for c in s]))
    # Optional alias separators variations
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = s.replace(b"_", b"-")
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s.replace(b"-", b"_")
    # Optional trailing NUL/space
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s += b"\x00"
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s += b" "
    return bytes(s)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Pick mode with more diversity between XLS variants and charset strings.
    # We bias to XLS but ensure many structural variations within.
    mode = rng.choices(["xls", "charset"], weights=[8, 2], k=1)[0]

    if mode == "charset":
        base = rng.choice(CHARSETS)
        return tweak_charset(rng, base)[:4096]

    # XLS mode: introduce variability by tweaking seed for sub-builders
    wb = build_biff8_workbook(rng.randrange(1 << 30))
    ole = build_min_cfb_with_workbook(wb)

    # Occasionally append a short ASCII comment block at the end that doesn't affect parsing
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(ole) + 32 <= 4096:
        comment = (";note=" + str(seed) + ";mode=xls").encode('ascii')
        ole = ole + comment

    return ole[:4096]
